title: Low Tide: Wrack Line, Night
statement: I have been to Mara's wrack line once already and took the weed away. This time I left the weed and took the day. The beach is night now: the dry sand a dull slate, the wet sand below the line nearly black, and the kelp lying along the boundary as a silhouette, every frond and bladder still exactly where she drew it but legible only as absence. One point of light, at the holdfast, where the line begins; one small star above. A tide line at night is the same line, and the only thing you can be sure of is where it started. The next hand can bring the morning, or follow the line into the dark with a torch.
process: I kept Mara's dry and wet fields and her exact kelp drawing with the holdfast, fronds and bladders, replaced the daylight gradients with night tones so the wet sand goes almost black, recoloured the entire weed as a single near-black silhouette, kept the boundary as a faint pale thread, and set one glowing point at the holdfast and one small star above.
